examples.title: Sign the calendar at the temple
examples.date: Qin period, late third century BCE

original.creator: Thies Staack
original.note: Transcription in Chinese characters from a joined administrative document. The bracketed explanation is supplied by the translator, and the interpretation of the calendar phrase is discussed in the edition.

translation.text: each personally make a note [about their visit] in the event calendar located at the temple.
translation.rightsNote: Short quotation of the credited English translation.

examples.context: Visitors to a temple were expected to write an entry in a record kept there. The document gives a specific example of Qin officials requiring written evidence of a visit.

sources.title: Thies Staack, Drafting, Copying, and Adding Notes, Bamboo and Silk 2 (2019), example 15

examples.title: Send cash and leave the summer clothes
examples.date: Qin period, late third century BCE
examples.place: Shuihudi cemetery, Yunmeng County, Hubei, China (approximate locality)

original.creator: Georgijs Dunajevs, in Lü Jing’s edition
original.note: Chinese-character transcription of the quoted request on the excavated letter. The article quotes an instruction relayed on Heifu’s behalf.

translation.text: Send me (Heifu) cash, do not bring summer clothes.
translation.translator: Georgijs Dunajevs, in Lü Jing’s edition
translation.rightsNote: CC BY 4.0. Short excerpt from the credited edition.

examples.context: While away from home, Heifu gets word to his family about what he needs. This line preserves the preference in plain terms. The letter’s carrier has not been established.

examples.title: Late for the feast, owe a beaker of wine
examples.place: Mogao Cave 17, near Dunhuang, Gansu, China

original.text: 如右(有)於時不到者，罰酒壹角。
original.creator: Imre Galambos, adapting Lionel Giles
original.note: Chinese-character transcription from the verso of a copy of the Diamond Sutra. Parentheses preserve the editor’s reading of a character.

translation.text: Those who do not arrive punctually will be fined one beaker (jiao) of wine
translation.rightsNote: Short quotation of the credited English translation.

examples.context: A local association asks its members to assemble near Jiejia Hermitage for an annual meeting and feast. The circular was passed among members, and a person who skipped the event entirely owed a larger fine.

sources.title: Imre Galambos, She Association Circulars from Dunhuang, pp. 860–861, translation adapted from Lionel Giles
International Dunhuang Programme, Late Tang association circular Or.8210/S.1453

examples.title: A debt of 105 denarii

original.creator: Roger S. O. Tomlin
original.note: Latin-letter transcription of writing incised into a waxed wooden tablet. Angle brackets and parentheses mark the editor’s additions or expansions.

translation.text: I owe Gratus the freedman of Spurius 105 denarii
translation.rightsNote: CC BY 4.0. Short excerpt from the credited edition.

examples.context: Tibullus acknowledges a debt to Gratus for merchandise already sold and delivered. Both men were freedmen. The tablet preserves its date and the amount owed.

sources.title: Roger S. O. Tomlin, Bloomberg London writing tablet 44

examples.title: The rate for hauling provisions

original.text:
penoris onera uiginti
in singula (denarii) quadṛạns uecturaẹ
original.creator: Roger S. O. Tomlin
original.note: Latin-letter transcription of the clause on quantity and freight. Parentheses expand a coin symbol, and dotted letters indicate uncertain traces.

translation.text: 20 loads of provisions at a transport-charge of one-quarter denarius for each
translation.rightsNote: CC BY 4.0. Short excerpt from the credited edition.

examples.context: Marcus Rennius Venustus records an agreement over a delivery from Verulamium. The contract specifies a November deadline and a charge per load.

examples.title: The soldiers have no beer

original.text:
ceruesam commilitones
non habunt quam
rogó iubeas mitti
original.creator: Alan K. Bowman and J. David Thomas
original.note: Latin-letter transcription of writing in Old Roman cursive, with spelling and the marked vowel as in the edition.

translation.text: My fellow-soldiers have no beer. Please order some to be sent.
translation.translator: Alan K. Bowman and J. David Thomas
translation.rightsNote: CC BY 4.0. Short excerpt from the credited edition.

examples.context: Masclus, a cavalry officer, asks his commander for instructions about the next day. He adds the request for beer after signing off. This wooden tablet predates Hadrian’s Wall.

sources.title: Alan K. Bowman and J. David Thomas, Vindolanda ink tablet 628
Roman Inscriptions of Britain, terms of use for texts and EpiDoc editions

examples.title: Wine, cheese and oil by the coin

original.text:
Vinum a(sse) S(emis)
Casium a(sse) S(emis)
Oleum a(sse) I
original.creator: Ancient Graffiti Project, principal contributor Holly Sypniewski and editor Rebecca Benefiel
original.note: Latin-letter transcription of a graffito, with editorial expansions in parentheses. The prices follow the current entry for this graffito.

translation.text: wine - 1/2 as, cheese - 1/2 as, oil - 1 as
translation.translator: Ancient Graffiti Project, principal contributor Holly Sypniewski and editor Rebecca Benefiel
translation.rightsNote: Short quotation of the credited English translation.

examples.context: Someone scratched a list of foods and prices on a column at Pompeii. The as was a small Roman coin. The writer and the purpose of the list are unknown.
